source.titleEnglishInternal: Talk with a regular over coffee
source.objectiveEnglishInternal: sustain a longer conversation about the neighborhood, work, and travel with follow-up questions
source.roleplayEnglishInternal: A retired regular asks where you're from; keep the conversation going for several turns, ask follow-ups, and close politely.

readerVerbExamples.target: Don Ramón platica con todos en el café.
readerVerbExamples.native: Don Ramón chats with everyone at the café.

archivedDraft.scene: A café regular starts a friendly conversation with a traveler at a shared table.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Friendly, affectionate form of café, very common in Mexico.
Pan dulce means the sweet pastries sold at Mexican bakeries.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: メキシコの菓子パン（パン・ドゥルセ）

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Estoy aquí de viaje por dos semanas.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: I'm here traveling for two weeks.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 私は2週間の旅行でここに来ています。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I'm here traveling for two weeks.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Hace cuánto tiempo vive en este barrio?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Use usted with an older person you just met.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: この近所にはどのくらい住んでいらっしゃいますか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: And what do you do for a living?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: それで、お仕事は何をされていますか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: And what do you do for a living?

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: An easy follow-up that keeps the conversation going.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 本当ですか？もっと聞かせてください。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: What do you recommend I visit around here?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: この辺りで、どこを訪ねるのがおすすめですか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: What do you recommend I visit around here?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Fue un placer platicar con usted.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: It was a pleasure chatting with you.
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: A polite way to end the conversation.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: お話しできて楽しかったです。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: It was a pleasure chatting with you.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Cada mañana, don Ramón, un jubilado y vecino del barrio, toma su cafecito en la misma mesa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Every morning, Don Ramón, a retiree and neighbor from the neighborhood, has his coffee at the same table.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 毎朝、退職者で近所の人でもあるドン・ラモンは、いつも同じテーブルでコーヒーを飲みます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Every morning, Don Ramón, a retiree and neighbor from the neighborhood, has his coffee at the same table.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Hoy me pregunta de dónde soy, y le digo: Soy de Canadá y estoy aquí de viaje por dos semanas.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Today he asks me where I'm from, and I tell him: I'm from Canada and I'm here traveling for two weeks.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 今日、彼は私にどこの出身かと尋ね、私は彼に言います。「カナダ出身です。2週間の旅行でここに来ています。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Today he asks me where I'm from, and I tell him: I'm from Canada and I'm here traveling for two weeks.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Luego le pregunto: ¿Hace cuánto tiempo vive en este barrio?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then I ask him: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: それから私は彼に尋ねます。「この近所にはどのくらい住んでいらっしゃいますか？」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Then I ask him: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Me cuenta que vive aquí desde hace 40 años y que era maestro en la escuela de la plaza.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He tells me that he has lived here for 40 years and that he was a teacher at the school on the plaza.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 彼は私に、ここに40年住んでいること、そして広場の学校で教師をしていたことを話してくれます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: He tells me that he has lived here for 40 years and that he was a teacher at the school on the plaza.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Como me interesa su trabajo, le digo: ¿De veras? Cuénteme más.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Since his work interests me, I say: Really? Tell me more.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 彼の仕事に興味があるので、私は言います。「本当ですか？もっと聞かせてください。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Since his work interests me, I say: Really? Tell me more.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después me habla del mercado, porque los sábados venden pan dulce muy bueno.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then he talks to me about the market, because on Saturdays they sell very good pan dulce.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: それから彼は市場のことを話してくれます。土曜日には、とてもおいしいパン・ドゥルセが売られているからです。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Then he talks to me about the market, because on Saturdays they sell very good pan dulce.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Cuando le pregunto qué me recomienda, dice que si tengo tiempo, debo visitar el museo del centro.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: When I ask him what he recommends, he says that if I have time, I should visit the downtown museum.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 何がおすすめかと尋ねると、彼は、時間があれば中心部の博物館に行くといいと言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: When I ask him what he recommends, he says that if I have time, I should visit the downtown museum.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Antes de irme, pago la cuenta y le digo: Fue un placer platicar con usted.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Before I leave, I pay the bill and tell him: It was a pleasure chatting with you.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 帰る前に、私は会計を済ませ、彼に言います。「お話しできて楽しかったです。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Before I leave, I pay the bill and tell him: It was a pleasure chatting with you.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Sustain a polite conversation with a retired café regular about travel, the neighborhood, former work and a local recommendation.
speakingGoalInternal: A retired regular asks where you're from; keep the conversation going for several turns, ask follow-ups, and close politely.
speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: カフェの常連であるドン・ラモンと話します。出身地と滞在期間を答え、近所や以前の仕事について質問し、おすすめを聞いて、丁寧に会話を終えてください。
sourceConflictInternal: The current eight-turn source is a first-person café conversation with retired neighborhood resident Don Ramón: traveler from Canada for two weeks, his forty years in the neighborhood and former teaching at the plaza school, Saturday pan dulce market, downtown museum recommendation, bill payment and polite close. The archived nine-turn dialogue substitutes a generic regular/traveler scene and invents a park, station and early-closing market. The source card asking what he does for a living has no Reader turn; do not invent one. Qualified Japanese, Mexican food, locale and dictionary review remains open.

savedPositionPolicy: Archived draft rows have no explicit stable row IDs and were not registered. Revision-scoped candidate IDs do not authorize saved-item or audio placement migration. Reordering requires a new revision.
reviewQuestionsInternal: Current source is a first-person narrative with Don Ramón, Canada, two weeks, forty years and the plaza school. Archived generic two-person dialogue changes the scene and is reference-only.

Source card cafecito is affectionate Mexican coffee wording; neutral Japanese コーヒー loses its diminutive. Qualified locale/dictionary reviewer should choose whether to preserve it in a note, without treating Spanish morphology as Japanese grammar.
Pan dulce is Mexican bakery sweet bread; メキシコの菓子パン（パン・ドゥルセ） identifies the food but food/locale review remains open.
The source card And what do you do for a living? is in the card list but not in the eight-turn Reader. Preserve the card without inventing a Reader conversation turn.
Town square/plaza is 広場; whether 町の広場 is preferred needs qualified review. Downtown museum is 中心部の博物館, not a new named venue.
The source Reader says Don Ramón was a teacher, but the card work is generic. The Japanese Reader keeps the past-tense teacher fact.

Retiree, neighbor, older-person register, direct Japanese speech, and polite closing require qualified Japanese review. The source does not require asking private details beyond the authored questions.
This is unapproved source-only draft; six authored modes, forms, speaking, contextual dictionary, saved-item policy, exact-text audio and distinct listening remain open.

Opus flagged 市場 reading ambiguity; the physical-market reading いちば must be pinned for eventual furigana and TTS, but this inert packet has no reading field. Fable agreed the issue belongs in review rather than silently changing the face.
